articles.title: Magnus Carlsen loses but Alpine Pipers enter GCL final
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: Grandmaster Alireza Firouzja crashed through the defences of World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen with the black pieces in 49 moves, as the French GM.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Grandmaster Alireza Firouzja crashed through the defences of World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen with the black pieces in 49 moves, as the French GM ensured Carlsen’s first defeat in this season’s Global Chess League on Saturday.It appeared Carlsen, playing for Alpine APL Pipers, would have his way, as in all the previous games here, but Firouzja came out firing on all cylinders by playing an aggressive line from the start. Carlsen led on the clock until around the 14th move but he missed a plot after that. Firouzja slowly tightened the screws as he ensured former champions Triveni Kings went out on a high. Magnus was two pawns down before he got into further trouble after Alireza exchanged the rooks. It was Alireza’s first win of the tournament and a first defeat for Carlsen.“It was a very sharp game, and I played, I think, not a bad game, and I put pressure on him, and then we went into trouble,” Alireza said.Pipers vs Ganges in finalWith Carlsen losing on the icon board and both their women Divya Desmukh and Koneru Humpy settling for draws, Alpine Pipers lost 6-11 to Triveni Kings, who were powered by Alireza and Aravindh Chithambaram who knocked down in-form player Vidit Gujrathi.Pipers were now in danger of missing a place in the final, with American Gambits breathing down their neck. But Gambits lost 6-11 to Mumba Masters.Candidates champion Javokhir Sindarov led the charge defeating Maxime Vachier-Lagrave with black pieces. But defeats to Nihal Sarin, Sara Khadem and Marc’Andria Maurizzi crushed their hopes, leaving the team with a dejected look in the dugout.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: From Glasgow setback to Nagoya challenge, Pranati Nayak aims to get it right this time at Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: KOLKATA: When Pranati Nayak gets ready to sprint down the runway at Nagoya City General Gymnasium during the Asian Games later this month, the memory .
articles.body: KOLKATA: When Pranati Nayak gets ready to sprint down the runway at Nagoya City General Gymnasium during the Asian Games later this month, the memory of Glasgow will inevitably return.At the Commonwealth Games, a lack of speed in her approach disrupted her first vault in the qualifying round, costing her valuable points and, ultimately, a place in the final.It was obviously not something one is used to seeing from Nayak and even left her long-time coach Ashok Mishra at a loss for words. “It was the first time I had seen her miss the running,” said Mishra.He, however, downplayed concerns over her injury, insisting that it was not what cost her in Glasgow. She had been dealing with plantar fasciitis — a problem underneath the foot that caused some pulling while running — but had competed with it before and even won a medal this year.Despite that, coach Mishra didn’t want to take any risks and made sure she got enough rest to prepare for her fourth Asian Games appearance, where she will compete only in the vault.“It is around 90-95% cured. Just 5% remains, and that is not a problem for her,” added Mishra. “After the Commonwealth Games, I gave her around three weeks of complete rest. So, she recovered. Otherwise, if we had continued training, it could have aggravated the injury.”But more importantly, the time helped her heal mentally.“She is now mentally much more mature. After everything, we just analyse it and focus on the next,” said Mishra. Also helping her stay focused are psychologists who not only talk to her but also help her with concentration exercises.Irrespective of that, one cannot deny that age is not on her side anymore and that it does make things difficult for the 31-year-old. Still, coach Mishra is confident that Nayak is all set for the challenge.That confidence is rooted in what Nayak has achieved since contemplating walking away from the sport after the Tokyo Olympics in 2021. She has since won two Asian Championship medals, two World Cup medals and one World Challenge Cup medal for India — a run that explains why Mishra still believes she has earned her place among the country’s best.But there is no doubt that the competition will be fierce at the Asian Games.China, Japan, North and South Korea and Chinese Taipei are among the leading gymnastics nations in the continent, while countries such as Philippines and Malaysia have also strengthened their programmes. The Korean gymnasts, in particular, are expected to pose a major challenge on vault.“It’s going to be a very difficult test for her. But I think she will do well. If she does both the 360-degree twist vaults cleanly with a fixed landing, then there is a very good possibility of her going to the final because execution matters,” said Mishra.Keeping this in mind, the coach has centred her training on reducing executional errors and improving explosive strength. To make sure she can do that, Nayak has been working on plyometrics, explosive leg-strength exercises and isometric muscle contractions.She has also been training on soft-landing equipment and in the foam pit, where the physical impact is reduced, before making the transition to the main landing area.For Mishra, that transition is as much mental as physical. “When it comes to the main landing area, it is much more difficult psychologically. You think about how heavy the impact will be,” he said.Nayak certainly has enough experience to make that shift at the right moment. After all, she remains India’s lone gymnast at the Asian Games for the second time in a row. And when she makes that run in Nagoya, the objective will be simple: get the approach right, execute the vault cleanly and, this time, make it to the final.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Red Sox move Sunday’s game time due to inclement weather
articles.summary: The Sox have announced that they are moving tomorrow’s game time to 3:05 PM due to inclement weather.
articles.body:
The Sox have announced that they are moving tomorrow's game time to 3:05 PM due to inclement weather.

A weather alert has been issued by the Boston 25 Weather team, with heavy rain and downpours expected throughout the area.

"The change was made in consultation with Major League Baseball due to a forecast for an extended period of rain throughout the morning and early afternoon," the Red Sox said. "The 3:05 p.m. start time corresponds with a projected window of improved weather conditions later in the afternoon and provides the best opportunity to play the game on Sunday."

The game, which was originally slated to start at 1:35 PM, will be the finale of a three-game series against the Royals. They dropped game 1 on Friday night with a 3-2 loss but took game 2 with a 5-1 win.

The Red Sox also announced that all tickets for tomorrow's game will be "good for admission at the newly scheduled time."

This is a developing story. Check back for updates as more information becomes available.

articles.title: Ted Cruz has just 2 words about curse after epic Texas comeback vs. Ohio State
articles.summary: Did Texas senator Ted Cruz really break the sports curse after Texas beat Ohio State?
articles.body:
After the College GameDay crowd booed Texas senator Ted Cruz , he got to watch the Longhorns engineer one heck of a comeback against top-ranked Ohio State. Texas beat the Buckeyes 24-23 after being down 20-3 at the half, with 21 unanswered points in the fourth quarter.

But does that mean that the so-called Ted Cruz curse is vanquished? After all, this has been a thing for years that fans in the Lone Star State have been citing for woes all around Texas. We can report that Cruz thinks so, with the senator posting just two words and a photo of himself with actor and Texas diehard Matthew McConaughey: "What curse?"

Here's the thing, though: Some fans think it was the presence of another politician that could have reversed the curse:

Fans think James Talarico helped break the Ted Cruz curse

articles.title: 'Alonso needs to find solutions quickly'
articles.summary: Sitting just a few rows behind Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, it was clear to see that he's still trying to find the answers when it comes to making this free-...
articles.body:
Sitting just a few rows behind Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, it was clear to see that he's still trying to find the answers when it comes to making this free-scoring side into a more solid team.

It was difficult not to have sympathy for Jorrel Hato , who had a nightmare first-half with some schoolboy defending to allow Hull City to equalise. It was no surprise to see him replaced at the break.

Even after that though, the Blues back-line looked nervous and the fans seemed nervy every time Hull City pushed forward. It also didn't help that Emi Martinez has not hit the ground running in a Chelsea number one shirt.

There are some excellent individual players in that Chelsea defence but - whether it's a back four or back three - Alonso needs to find solutions quickly or there is no way they'll be able to keep pace with some of the more complete teams at the top end of the Premier League.

It must be getting frustrating for their amazing attacking players who are certainly delivering so far in this campaign.
authors: John Bennett - BBC Final Score reporter at Stamford Bridge

articles.title: Kosgei wins Great North Run but McColgan withdraws
articles.summary: Kenya's Brigid Kosgei wins the women's race at the Great North Run as Eilish McColgan drops out early with injury, while American Zouhair Talbi wins the men'...
articles.body:
Kenya's Brigid Kosgei achieved a convincing victory in the women's race at the Great North Run after Great Britain's Eilish McColgan withdrew with injury.

McColgan, 35, was continuing her return to racing after recovering from a broken toe, but she suffered a foot injury early in the half-marathon and limped off.

Kosgei, an Olympic silver medallist and former London marathon winner, eased to the win in one hour, six minutes and 15 seconds.

Despite that being slower than the course record of 1:04:28 she set seven years ago, Kosgei, 32, dominated from the start and ran much of the 13.1-mile race solo.

She crossed the line over two minutes quicker than compatriot and last year's winner Sheila Chepkirui in second place.

Amy-Eloise Neale was the first British athlete to finish, coming fifth overall.

McColgan, who finished third in last year's Great North Run, suffered the toe injury during the London Marathon in April where she was the first British athlete to finish, taking seventh place.

The Scot had blood seeping through her shoe as she crossed the line and subsequently had to miss the Commonwealth Games in July.

She made her comeback in last week's Big Half in London and won that race in 1:10:54, but McColgan admitted afterwards that she was still concerned about the injury and her fitness.

American Zouhair Talbi produced a brilliant kick in the final mile to win the men's race as he got the better of last year's champion Alex Mutiso.

The pair were running side by side for most of the course before 31-year-old Talbi surged ahead in the closing stages and held on to win in 59:47.

He narrowly missed out on beating his personal best of 59:41.

Mutiso finished 14 seconds behind Talbi in 1:00:01.

Yohei Ikeda of Japan came third, while Marc Scott - who won the race in 2021 - was the first British athlete to finish in eighth place.

The course record of 58:56 for the men's race has stood since 2011, and was set by Martin Mathathi of Kenya.

Britain's David Weir won his 10th Great North Run title in the men's wheelchair race as he finished in 43:06, while Melanie Woods was the women's winner in 50:19.

This year's race is the 45th edition and an estimated 63,000 runners took part, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

articles.title: Lothar Matthäus confident Harry Kane should win Ballon d’Or
articles.summary: Matthäus feels the Ballon d’Or belongs to FC Bayern’s Harry Kane
articles.body:
It really depends on who you'd ask, but Bayern Munich and England's Harry Kane is a serious shout to win this year's Ballon d'Or at the end of next month at the London Palladium. France Football's certainly no stranger to making controversial decisions in doling out what's historically been the most prestigious inidivual honor for a footballer, but there's massive hope for the England skipper after an absolutley sensational season for club and country.

For the time frame the Ballon d'Or is judged on, Kane was incredibly lethal for Bayern and England, and there's simply no denying that. Last season, Kane finished with 61 goals and 7 assists from a total of 51 appearances across all competitions. For England at the World Cup, the Three Lions' skipper tallied 6 goals and 1 assist in their run to the semifinals before getting knocked out by Argentina. Had England gone on to the final and beaten Spain, Kane would surely be the odds-on favorite to win the Ballon d'Or without any trace of doubt.

While Kane does have some competition from the likes of Kylian Mbappé , Lamine Yamal , Rodri , Ousmane Dembélé , Khvicha Kvaratskhelia , and perhaps even Fabián Ruiz, former Bayern and Germany midfielder Lothar Matthäus, Kane is the favorite to win.

"For me, Harry Kane is the favorite to win the Ballon d'Or. Why? German champion, DFB Pokal winner, Champions League semi-finalist, third place at the World Cup. He performed in every single competition, scored goals, was a leader for his teams. He's a difference maker. His character on and off the pitch is impeccable – for me being a role model is also an important factor in winning the Ballon d'Or," Matthäus rationalized to Bild Tv (via @iMiaSanMia ).

In terms of his direct competitors, Matthäus knows that there have been some incredible achievements in big moments from those players, but that Kane has delivered the highest performances overall as a collective. The award is reportedly placing an emphasis on popping up with key moments in big matches, but it's clear that Kane has done that, and then some.

"All other nominees won things as well – but when you look at the performance as a whole, Harry Kane is the frontrunner and has a very big chance of winning it. I'd be happy for him, not because he's a Bayern player, but because he's an excellent ambassador of international football," Matthäus stressed.

articles.title: 'Core of Hull's promoted team vital for team spirit and togetherness'
articles.summary: Regan Slater told me pre-match that togetherness and getting the basics right were the key factors to Hull City getting something out of a game against free-...
articles.body:
Regan Slater told me pre-match that togetherness and getting the basics right were the key factors to Hull City getting something out of a game against free-scoring Chelsea .

The Tigers stalwart was spot on and, along with his team-mates, he certainly delivered. I'm sure I wasn't the only one in the press box thinking that after the Morgan Rogers 's early goal, it would be a comfortable home win on Saturday.

But, this Hull side under Sergei Jakirovic is made of stronger stuff. Yes defensive mistakes helped get them back into the game, but it was also their work-rate and confidence that put a vulnerable Chelsea back-line under pressure. Then, after Mohamed Belloumi's two goals, Hull City didn't sit back and constantly looked dangerous on the break, even after Joao Pedro 's equaliser.

Despite all the new signings, eight of the starting XI on Saturday were Hull players last season and that core of the promoted team seems vital when it comes to the amazing team spirit and togetherness.

But the new players, many who came off the bench at Stamford Bridge, are adding a new dimension too.

Slater called Jakirovic "class" after the game and the Hull City manager is certainly getting everything right at the moment, with this mix of new and longer serving players, when it comes to defying the Premier League odds.
authors: John Bennett - BBC Final Score reporter at Stamford Bridge

articles.title: SEC power rankings have a new No. 1 after Week 2
articles.summary: Texas takes the top spot from Georgia in the SEC power rankings after a massive comeback win against Ohio State in Week 2.
articles.body:
The No. 3 Texas Longhorns and quarterback Arch Manning earned an impressive comeback win over the No. 1 Ohio State Buckeyes. Texas dominated in the fourth quarter to overcome a 20-point deficit at home. Texas earned the country's most impressive win of the season and replaces the Georgia Bulldogs , who have not played a Power Four team yet, as the No. 1 team in our SEC power rankings after Week 2.

Across the SEC, Texas A&M, Missouri, Mississippi State and Tennessee all defeated Power Four opponents by over 14 points. Alabama won 45-17 thanks to a dominant second half over the Kentucky Wildcats in Alabama's SEC opener.

The Oklahoma Sooners fell on the road to the Michigan Wolverines in a defensive showdown, which serves as a blow to Oklahoma's playoff hopes. Utah demolished Arkansas, who looks like the worst team in the SEC.

Georgia , South Carolina, LSU, Ole Miss and more all won comfortably over inferior opponents to move to 2-0. Vanderbilt had a slight scare against Delaware in a nine-point game. The SEC has looked strong in nonconference play with just two SEC teams suffering nonconference losses thus far.

articles.title: Texas football spent years chasing this moment. It just changed everything | Opinion
articles.summary: Arch Manning and Texas overcame a 20-point deficit to beat Ohio State in the greatest comeback in school history.
articles.body:
AUSTIN, TX – Here's your turning point, everyone. For Texas, for Arch Manning , for Steve Sarkisian.

All it took was the greatest comeback in Texas history.

It begins with No. 1 Ohio State blowing a 20-point second half lead , and Texas scoring in the final, frantic seconds to complete an unimaginable comeback. But the 24-23 Texas win was so much more than that.

It was two teams with $50 million rosters trading blows. It was All-American plays and unthinkable mistakes, turnovers and fourth-down gambles, a missed late field goal and a game-winning touchdown from the 1 that, fortunately for Texas, took three plays — and ran enough clock to keep the Ohio State offense off the field for more than desperate seconds.

It was 21 points in the fourth quarter for a Texas offense that couldn't string together first downs, and dropped a touchdown pass. It was a comeback for the ages that Texas and the SEC needed, that Sarkisian orchestrated and Manning executed and the next thing you know, the narrative is now about Ohio State coach Ryan Day losing his past three big games. It was the first time since 2004 that an AP No. 1-ranked team blew a 20-point lead in the fourth quarter, a span of 197 games.

That enough from 60 minutes of football?

"I told Ryan, I hope we see you again," Sarkisian said.

Texas Longhorns and Ohio State Buckeyes meet in Austin

The next time would be the College Football Playoff, but let's slow this thing down before it gets loose again. Because that's where it was prior to this moment: Texas thinking and dreaming big, but with plenty of heartache and missed opportunity to show for it since joining the SEC.

The blown lead to Georgia in the 2024 SEC championship game. The fumbled return for a touchdown that sealed Ohio State's 2024 CFP semifinal win. And the ugly loss to the Buckeyes in 2025.

So what did Texas get from this rare, hard-to-believe moment? Not much, especially with a brutal SEC schedule on the horizon. There's Oklahoma and Ole Miss and LSU and Texas A&M and Missouri , and that's just the beginning.

With so much buildup. They went all-in this offseason, spending big in the transfer portal to put pieces around Manning and allow him to reach his talented ceiling. Sarkisian spoke all offseason about this team and this moment.

Then Texas went out and played its worst half in years. Two of its first five plays were turnovers that led to Ohio State points, and that was soon followed by a disastrous fourth-down decision that led to more Ohio State points.

By the time the Ohio State defense got another stop in the third quarter, another long drive led to three more points and a 20-point Buckeyes lead. This thing screamed same ol' Texas.

"There was no way I was coming back (to the post-game news conference) and hearing that," Manning said afterward.

Same ol' Texas rolled off three touchdown drives of 91, 72 and 73 yards in the fourth quarter to blow it all to pieces. To put that in perspective: Texas finished with 336 total yards — and had 236 on the final three scoring drives.

Manning completed 11 of his last 15 passes (he was 12 of 22 prior), and had critical scrambles for first downs and positive momentum. The run game showed up, and forced the Ohio State defense to commit more on defense, sustain 40 plays over those last three drives alone (38 total plays prior), and my god, this is really happening, isn't it?

An Ohio State offense that did whatever it wanted, that ran the ball with force and consistency, that had the best player on the field in wideout Jeremiah Smith — who Texas couldn't cover for 50 minutes — suddenly couldn't move the ball.

Texas tried everything to stop Smith, who had two plays of 40-plus yards and eight catches for 164 yards. They tried bracketing him with a safety, tried rolling coverage to his side of the field. They tried zone and matchup zone.

Finally, new Texas defensive coordinator Will Muschamp decided to go man coverage in the fourth quarter. They were getting beat every other way, why not the one way where it could get much uglier.

Only it didn't. Smith didn't catch a pass in the fourth quarter, and was only targeted three times — including two Hail Mary heaves on the final drive of the game.

"They defense got the ball back each time," said Texas offensive tackle Trevor Goosby. "You can't overlook that. Without that, where are we?"

Right back where they were last season, wondering how a loss to Ohio State could impact the rest of the season. Only this time, they're on the other side of it — and they've moved the SEC one step closer to knocking the Big Ten from the big chair of college football.

Texas needed it, but so did the SEC. Oklahoma's loss to wayward Michigan earlier in the day was a gut punch for the once mighty league.

Another Texas loss to Ohio State — especially the way it was unfolding over the first three quarters — would've been disastrous for the league's suddenly shaky standing. All of that changed in one wild quarter.

'We can't play like we did in the first half and expect to win in our league," Sarkisian said.

Remember, this was the line in the sand for Sarkisian, who spent all offseason complaining about the CFP selection committee — and declaring that, but for the loss to Ohio State last year, Texas would've been in the playoff. So why play the game?

This is why you play the game. Because it can change everything.

Matt Hayes is the senior national college football writer for USA TODAY Sports Network. Follow him on X at @MattHayesCFB . Listen to him daily, from 12-2 p.m., on 1010XL-Jacksonville .

articles.title: What Adam Amin is most excited to see from Bears offense vs. Panthers
articles.summary: FOX announcer Adam Amin revealed what excites him the most about the Chicago Bears offense coming into this season.
articles.body:
There are many layers to the Chicago Bears offense that makes them an intriguing unit coming into the 2026 season, but it's not all about quarterback Caleb Williams .

With plenty of focus on the rushing attack that was one of the best in the NFL last season, as well as young wide receivers Rome Odunze and Luther Burden , there's been some overlooking of the tight end group as a whole.

Adam Amin, who will be on the broadcast for the Bears regular season opener against the Carolina Panthers , revealed that he's most focused on how head coach Ben Johnson will use the tight end group this year. Led by Colston Loveland who is expected to be a big breakout candidate this year, Amin thinks there will be plenty of unique looks on offense.

"Offensively, it's tight end usage," Amin told 104.3 The Score . "It'll be fascinating to see the continuing trend in the league to go bigger on offense to combat the big defenders on the other side. You may have five or six teams that go 15%+ in terms of three tight end usage. A player like Colston Loveland has a lot of growth opportunity here because he's a great in-line blocking tight end, and he can step out and play a Z receiver in a couple of formations."

The Bears could and most certainly will be expected to use their top three tight ends: Loveland, veteran Cole Kmet , and rookie Sam Roush, in a multitude of ways this season. All three can make impacts in the run-blocking game, but all three are also very capable of making plays with the ball in their hands as receivers. Although, none greater than Loveland, who led the team with 713 receiving yards last season.

articles.title: “Should be Ashamed”: Skip Bayless Launches Scathing Attack on Ryan Day-led Ohio State Staff and Players After Texas Debacle
articles.summary: In a weekend filled with upsets, the No. 4 Texas Longhorns took down the No.
articles.body:
In a weekend filled with upsets, the No. 4 Texas Longhorns took down the No. 1 Ohio State Buckeyes 24-23. The game was the biggest comeback for Texas since 2007, in an encounter that seemed to be getting away from them in the first half.

Steve Sarkisian's men crammed a game's worth of action into the last quarter of the encounter. Up until the end of the third quarter, the Longhorns had only managed to score three points while the Buckeyes had scored 23. It was in the fourth quarter that Arch Manning and the Longhorns scored 21 unanswered points.

While it's an amazing feat by Texas, it's also a bit negligent by Ohio State to have allowed such a score to get away from them. At least, that's what Skip Bayless seems to think:

"That game was 23-3 after 3 quarters. THE Ohio State should be ashamed – coaches and players," wrote Bayless on X.

What's most surprising is that Arch Manning didn't even win the quarterback battle in Austin this Saturday night. Manning threw for 196 yards, with one touchdown pass and an interception, while completing 62.1% of his passes.

For his part, Julian Sayin threw for 278 yards, also with one touchdown and an interception, while completing 53.1% of his passes.

Quarterback Arch Manning on Texas victory over Ohio State

While running around the field after securing the victory, signal-caller Arch Manning stopped for a moment to talk with ESPN's Laura Rutledge and express his feelings about Texas's victory. He admitted he was incredibly happy, but also shared the honor of the victory with his teammates:

"It felt good," the Texas quarterback said. "We have a bunch of good players, a lot of leaders. It's gonna be a fun night," said Manning immediately after the game ended

"I'm so proud of our guys in all three phases. It wasn't very pretty, but we found a way to win. That's what good teams do."

Arch Manning also said last year's game against Ohio State weighed on his shoulders. In Week 1 of the 2025 season, the Longhorns fell to the Buckeyes in a game at Columbus, Ohio, for which Manning was heavily criticized.

articles.title: Arrowhead pulls away from Brookfield East with powerful second half
articles.summary: Arrowhead scored 36 points after halftime to turn a close game into a runaway.
articles.body:
Brookfield East took an early lead and held a 14-9 advantage at halftime before Arrowhead's offense came alive in the second half. The Warhawks scored 14 points in the third quarter and 22 in the fourth to turn the game into a 45-21 victory Sept. 11 at Pfeiffer Memorial Field at Taraska Stadium in Hartland.

Arrowhead scored three points in the first quarter before Brookfield East answered with 14 points in the second quarter. The Warhawks responded with two rushing touchdowns in the third quarter and added a two-point conversion to take a 23-14 lead entering the fourth.

Lucas Yttre passed for 178 yards and two touchdowns for Brookfield East in the losing effort. Beau Evans caught five passes for 113 yards and two TDs.

The Warhawks improved to 4-0, while Brookfield East fell to 2-2. The teams also met in the WIAA playoffs last season, where Arrowhead rallied late to defeat Brookfield East, 31-29.

articles.title: Gladbach begin search for new head coach with Eichner mentioned in early conversations
articles.summary: The club officially announced Polanski’s departure after a run of three defeats from their opening three fixtures, during which they conceded 12 goals. His e...
articles.body:
The club officially announced Polanski's departure after a run of three defeats from their opening three fixtures, during which they conceded 12 goals. His exit brings his tenure to an end after just under a year in charge.

Attention will now turn towards finding his replacement, with the new head coach tasked with generating some positive feeling around the club and guiding them away from the wrong end of the table. In the early stages of their search, Bild has named former Karlsruher SC boss Christian Eichner as a candidate. Eichner left the 2. Bundesliga side at the end of last season following a six-year reign.

Previously, the also-unattached Ole Werner, most recently of RB Leipzig , Horst Steffen, most recently of Werder Bremen , and Alexander Blessin, most recently of St. Pauli , had also been linked with Gladbach .

Assistant coach Jan-Moritz Lichte will take over on an interim basis, with the bottom-of-the-table side set to face Mainz 05 on Saturday.

articles.title: Jaxson Dart holds Giants’ future in his hands, wants to do ‘something special’
articles.summary: Dart is set to make first Week 1 start of his NFL career on Sunday vs. Cowboys.
articles.body:
John Harbaugh is the biggest reason for the optimism around the New York Giants entering the 2026 season.

Jaxson Dart , though, holds the key to just how bright the Giants' future might be.

This is something I said this week during an appearance on the ' NFC East Mixtape ' podcast:

"Everything starts for the Giants with John Harbaugh. You guys know what the Giants have been for the last 12, 13 years. It hasn't been pretty. It has mostly not been enjoyable. There are warts on John Harbaugh's resume from Baltimore . We know that. But John Harbaugh brought credibility. He brought culture. He brought leadership. He brought professionalism and an idea for how to build a football team that this organization badly needed. So everything changes with John Harbaugh. Everything starts with John Harbaugh.

"It doesn't go where the Giants want it to go unless Jaxson Dart is what they think he can be at some point in the future. So, it starts with with Harbaugh, but if they're going to get where they want to be, it runs through Jaxson Dart."

Dart's potential is one of the reasons Harbaugh took the Giants job. In a fascinating sitdown with former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin, Harbaugh said Dart is "even more talented than I thought he was."

"When you watch a player every day in practice, you get a sense of what he's capable of doing. He can really throw it," Harbaugh told Tomlin. "He really has a great pocket presence. He understands the pocket. He feels it. He also sees downfield. Then he can get out and move and he can make plays. He's got a patience and poise about him."

That doesn't mean Dart, a second-year quarterback with 12 NFL starts on his resume, is where the Giants need him to be.

"He's learning," Harbaugh said. "Our coaches are doing a great job with him every single day. He's got to find a way to be tight and refined like all the quarterbacks do. But you don't want to take away. You never took it away from Ben [ Roethlisberger ] … "… There's times that they'll just they'll look at you and you'll know. It's like, "Hey, man, I trust you." You go be you."

"He's learning," Harbaugh said. "Our coaches are doing a great job with him every single day. He's got to find a way to be tight and refined like all the quarterbacks do. But you don't want to take away. You never took it away from Ben [ Roethlisberger ] …

"… There's times that they'll just they'll look at you and you'll know. It's like, "Hey, man, I trust you." You go be you."

In his annual quarterback rankings , Chris Simms of NBC Sports had Dart at No. 22. That is one spot ahead of Cam Ward of the Tennessee Titans , and one spot behind Jalen Hurts of the Philadelphia Eagles .

In an exclusive interview with Big Blue View, Simms said his biggest long-term question about Dart is whether he will ever be an elite thrower of the football.

"Dart's got unreal feel and instincts, right. And his ability to extend plays and play backyard football is really where he's special, and really a part of his game that I did not see that coming from what I evaluated in college," Simms said. "He's a pretty good decision-maker.

"I like his arm. I'm just saying I don't know if it's elite. I'm not sure it's an elite arm. It's a real good arm."

Simms said Dart "hits the throws that are there to be made." Simms just isn't certain the 23-year-old can make the special throws that separate some of the elite quarterbacks.

"Do I think he can make some of the high level throws that I would say the elite guys in the sport right now can make? Mahomes , Allen, Burrow, Lamar, Justin Herbert , Caleb Williams , Matthew Stafford ," Simms said. "Those guys make five or six throws a game where I go, no, you don't understand there. Nobody in football made those five or six throws today. That was a special play or throw or the ability to kind of slide in the pocket and throw a 25-yard laser on the right sideline into a window where, a lot of quarterbacks, you go, well, don't even throw that. Don't even do that.

"That's just one area I think that I'd like to see a little bit more of, and be proven that he can do that on a consistent basis. And I guess I just haven't seen that yet."

Dart will be asked to play under center much more this season than he did as a rookie. The offense will emphasize play-action throws from the pocket. Dart wasn't asked to do that often last season, and wasn't great at it when it was required. Dart completed just 57.3% of play-action passes in 2025, 24th of 26 qualifying quarterbacks, per Pro Football Focus.

Early in training camp, Dart said the Giants had " repped the hell out of " under center, play-action. It is something we continued to see him spend a large amount of time working on during each practice throughout the summer.

Perhaps the under center work is part of helping Dart become "tight and refined" as a quarterback.

"I don't know how much he's done it [under center], but he looks good doing it. It hasn't been an issue at all," Harbaugh said. "I would say, under center in the passing game, it does really discipline your footwork because the drops are so important under center. I think it enhances – he would tell you it helps even in the gun, in the pistol, or whatever. It's just another element."

Simms believes playing under center, with the increased respect defenses have to give the run game and play-action, will be good for Dart.

"The greatest thing is it's the best way to create explosive plays on the field right now is play action pass," Simms said. "We're at an era where it's very weird, where explosive plays are actually probably at this point, more indicative of who's going to win the game rather than turnover margin.

"So that's again, where those big throws that we talk about and all that, I think they have more value now in the NFL than ever before, because the defenses are just so good. They're so talented. It's too hard to say, Oh yeah, we're going to drive 12 plays, 75 yards all game long. There's going to be a strip sack. There's going to be a tip pass interception. So, you need to be able to make those explosive plays."

Simms said Dart is "made for" the kind of offense the Giants are implementing. There is one caveat. Can he make the difficult throws from the pocket?

"Within that play action pass thing, I think we will get to [see] what you're talking about, where, yeah, we're going to see if he can make some of those big explosive plays into tight windows, because I think it's going to be asked of him more this year than it was maybe last year," Simms said.

Jon Runyan Jr . spilled the beans regarding an interesting text Dart sent to his offensive linemen a few days ago, per the New York Post . It read:

"I want to be the best quarterback in the world.''

Dart certainly isn't that right now. He will probably never be. Simms has no issue with the goal.

"I have no problems with him telling his teammates and stuff like that," Simms said "I respect the guy that puts himself out there like that and almost puts pressure on himself and expectations. He lets everybody know.

"Your great quarterbacks are all really wired that way … I do respect that confidence and a little bit of the burden of, hey, look, I'm trying to be something special here. So I hope that makes guys want to be a part of that."

It's no surprise that Simms said Dart won't get there unless he does a better job protecting himself.

"The first thing is you can't be in the top 10 [among quarterbacks] if you're hurt every other week," Simms said. "So let's just start there.

"As you know, the best ability is availability. So, we can't be taking some of these hits. He's got to realize that the extra three yards are not worth what his value is to the team. That's part of being the unselfish quarterback. That's what you got to do."

Simms believes the talent is there for Dart to be a top 10 quarterback.

"I really think he's got everything," Simms said. "I just want to see a few more of those in the pocket game-changing difference type of throws."

Sunday's will be Dart's first NFL season-opening start.

"I think that I've just been waiting for this," Dart said. "I think this is just the coolest stage, the coolest opportunity to play in front of our fans, Sunday night football against a team like the Cowboys and go out there and compete and it's going to be an electric atmosphere and I can't wait to be a part of it."

Dart feels like a better player than he was as a rookie.

"I feel like I'm not even the same person at all. Obviously, the growth that you make from the experiences that you have from one year to the next. And I just feel like I've grown a ton through this offseason," he said. "So, I feel comfortable. I feel like I'm seeing things really well. And this is going to be a really good test for our team and with a team like the Cowboys are going to be really competitive."

There is a long way to go, though, for Dart to be what he wants to be. And what the Giants need him to be. Dart has been willing to put in the work.

"I think anytime that you are really pushing yourself to your limits on end, I think that's where and really in any profession, whatever you're doing, you're going to grow the most," Dart said. "That was an emphasis that I really wanted to put on myself coming into year two. Having a different situation than last, where this year I was the guy and I want to take the necessary steps to go out there. And I think that there's a ton of extra motivation from this past season. And I want to do something special."

"So, whatever it takes, that's the same that we say in the locker room all the time. So, it doesn't matter the time that you got to put in, whatever it takes to win and whatever it takes for you to be ultimately your best is required day in and day out."

articles.title: “Inexcusable”: Emmanuel Acho Not Convinced By Michigan’s Win Over Oklahoma Despite Kyle Whittingham’s 2-0 Start
articles.summary: Emmanuel Acho isn’t completely convinced by Michigan’s 17-10 win over Oklahoma. The Wolverines moved to 2-0 under head coach Kyle Whittingham, but their offe...
articles.body:
Emmanuel Acho isn't completely convinced by Michigan 's 17-10 win over Oklahoma . The Wolverines moved to 2-0 under head coach Kyle Whittingham, but their offensive numbers left plenty to be desired.

Acho believes that the result says as much about Oklahoma's struggles as it does about Michigan's second straight win. The former NFL star took to X to share his thoughts on the game. He posted his comments with a screenshot of the game's box score.

"That's a disgusting loss for Oklahoma. But it's even more inexcusable when you look at Michigan's box score," Acho wrote .

Michigan managed just 263 total yards, while Bryce Underwood completed only 9 of 17 passes for 111 yards. The Wolverines also failed to record a passing touchdown. Despite those struggles, they still found a way to win.

According to Acho, Michigan's offense was subpar, and while Oklahoma's defense did a good job, their offense let the team down.

At the postgame press conference, Oklahoma coach Brent Venables talked about his team's performance. Venables believes the loss won't severely affect the players' mindset, and they'll be ready for the challenges ahead.

"It's no more difficult than it was two weeks ago," he said, per ESPN . "It's the same schedule, and our guys are ready for it. They understand the challenge. … They're not going to be fearful of, 'all of a sudden you lost a one-score game on the road in front of 107,000 people. We had an opportunity late with the ball to go down and tie it up. There's no worry, doubt, or fatalistic mindset. That's not this locker room."

Oklahoma will play New Mexico , Georgia, and Texas in their next three games.

Kyle Whittingham on Bryce Underwood's Performance

While Bryce Underwood's passing numbers were underwhelming in Week 2 as well, he made an impact on the ground, rushing for 87 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries, including a 38-yard score.

After the game, Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham said that it was part of the plan to utilize Underwood as a runner.

"It was part of the plan," he said , per SB Nation. "We still understand that we need to get the throw game into higher gear and get more production there."

Whittingham said that Underwood's performance in Week 2 was "much better," and if he continues to get better like this, the Michigan Wolverines would be a tough team to beat.

articles.title: ESPN's Rich Eisen picks Detroit Lions to win NFC North title
articles.summary: Rich Eisen is rolling with the Detroit Lions as his preseason pick to win the NFC North.
articles.body:
ESPN's Rich Eisen named the Detroit Lions as his projected NFC North winner on a recent airing of "The Rich Eisen Show," as the crew outlined how they believe the highly competitive division will play out this year.

Instead of rattling off statistics and analytics, Eisen kept the rationale for putting the Lions at the top of his NFC North projections straightforward.

"I went with the Lions at one, Eisen said. "I think Jahmyr Gibbs is gonna do what everybody expects. I think (Jared) Goff 's gonna come back. I think the offense is gonna be better. And I think defensively, finally, you know, let's just have the football Gods stop kicking them in the injury nards, man."

The University of Michigan graduate added that one of the biggest reasons behind Detroit's subpar 9-8 record last season was the inadequate replacement at offensive coordinator.

"I'm just saying last year their plan to replace Ben Johnson didn't work out. They needed a better plan for that," Eisen said. "Their plan was definitely not 'Let's switch coordinators midseason and have Dan Campbell.'"

As for the rest of the division, Eisen slotted the Chicago Bears second, the Minnesota Vikings third, and the Green Bay Packers to finish last at No. 4.

The Lions will look to prove Eisen right when they open their regular-season slate on Sunday, Sept. 13, at Ford Field against the New Orleans Saints . Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET, and the game will be broadcast by Fox.

For more Lions coverage, follow us on X, @TheLionsWire , and give our Facebook page a like . Follow Scout on X: @SpringgateNews

articles.title: NFL power rankings, updated entering Sunday Week 1
articles.summary: Entering Sunday of NFL Week 1, these are the power rankings for all 32 teams.
articles.body:
Welcome to the 2026 NFL Season. As we head into the first Sunday of the season, we have already seen a couple of games and have already suffered a couple of injuries. Let's run down the entire league and see where all 32 teams stand as we kick off our first full Sunday of football.

Jan 22, 2026; Miami Gardens, FL, USA; Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley, right, joined by general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan, left, speak to reporters during their introductory press conference at Baptist Health Training Complex. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images

#32 Miami Dolphins: This is going to be a learning year for new head coach Jeff Hafley as he works with a roster that will be hamstrung by $180m in dead cap money.

#31 Cleveland Browns : Will it be Watson or Shadeur? It doesn't matter much; this offense is going to be led by one of the worst QBs in the league either way. The defense is decent, but losing Miles Garrett is going to sting.

#30 Arizona Cardinals : They could have a top-5 offense, but they will certainly have a bottom-5 defense. This team should be fun to watch, but it's hard to project more than 3 or 4 wins.

#29 Washington Commanders : They are pinning their hopes on Jayden Daniels staying healthy, but that's easier said than done. The defense is mediocre at best, and this offense is going to feel the loss of Larami Tunsil.

#28 Las Vegas Raiders : Klint Kubiak is going to turn this team around, but it's probably not going to happen right away. Losing Brock Bowers just days before the opening for a few weeks is less than ideal.

#27 New York Jets : Geno Smith is going to settle the offense down, and the defense is going to get better as the year progresses. The upside for this squad is close to .500, but it feels like they are going to need to draft their franchise QB and find their head coach next offseason.

#26 Atlanta Falcons : They changed coaches, but didn't do anything else to make the team better. The defense is going to suffer between the injury to Jalen Walker and the suspension of James Pierce, and the offense is going to struggle without a QB.

#25 New York Giants : John Harbaugh comes to town bringing tons of experience. Translate that to an old coaching staff that would be a great fit for a team on the verge of taking the next step. That's not this roster quite yet, so expect mixed results this season.

#24 Tennessee Titans : A new coaching staff comes in to shepherd their top pick QB for his sophomore campaign. Things could be getting better in Nashville, but this division is still multiple steps ahead of the Titans right now.

#23 Carolina Panthers : Will Bryce Young ever take the next step? This is a big prove-it year for both the QB and his head coach.

#22 Pittsburgh Steelers : They have an old QB and replaced their old coach with another old coach. They may be good enough to win the North, but it feels like the upside here is limited to maybe one playoff game at best.

#21 Indianapolis Colts : If Daniel Jones can make it all the way back to how he was playing before the injuries last season, this team could make some noise and challenge for the South Division crown. They need their cornerbacks to live up to their reputation for the defense to be a factor.

Aug 28, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough (6) warms up before the game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images

#20 New Orleans Saints: Kellen Moore might have his QB in Tyler Shough. If the offense takes a step forward, this team has a real shot at winning their division.

#19 Tampa Bay Buccaneers : The team paid both Vita Vea and Baker Mayfield to clear either of those contract talks from being a distraction. It feels like it would have been smarter to let Baker play angry. The team is decent, not great, but that might be plenty to win the NFC South.

#18 Green Bay Packers : There are still a ton of question marks surrounding this team. The offensive line is suspect, their starting running back is in limbo awaiting a suspension, and they are waiting on Micah Parsons to return on defense.

#17 Kansas City Chiefs : The Power of Mahomes and Reid will compel them to a winning record. It may just be 9-8, but it will be a winning record.

#16 Cincinnati Bengals : The defense is better, and Joe Burrow is healthy. The range of outcomes for this team is anywhere between a deep playoff push and a top 10 pick in next year's draft. Their success is directly tied to that first sentence remaining true all season.

#15 Chicago Bears : They have a great offense with a great offensive coach. They are going to struggle to get deep into the playoffs with this defense, but they will be fun to watch this year.

#14 San Francisco 49ers : They traveled down under and came away with an opening week victory. In the process, they lost rookie D'Zhaun Stribling, and this team is going to really struggle if the injury bug is going to torment them again all season.

#13 Minnesota Vikings : Brian Flores' defense is going to keep them in games, and if Kyler Murray can just be adequate, this team is going to challenge to win the NFC North.

#12 Los Angeles Chargers : The offensive line was a huge issue last season. With both tackles back and fully healthy and with new OC Mike McDaniels calling the plays, Justin Herbert may have his best year ever.

#11 Detroit Lions : The window to win a championship feels like it has closed considerably in Detroit. It will be interesting if Drew Petzig coming in as the new OC will have a positive effect, as there are still some questions regarding the offensive line. Week 1 will be a good test as they host the Saints.

Aug 13, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (10) warms up before a preseason game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Natalie Reid-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

#10 New England Patriots: The good news is they don't have to play the Seahawks again this year unless we get a Super Bowl rematch. The bad news is we don't know if Drake Maye has now been figured out by the league.

#9 Houston Texans : This is easily one of the best defenses in the league, and if they can avoid mistakes on offense, they will be a problem for the rest of the AFC. Demeco Ryans is sticking with CJ Stroud for now, but don't be shocked if the leash is short, as Davis Mills has shown he can manage a game plan.

#8 Dallas Cowboys: The defense was the worst in the league last year. Improvements were made, and if they can just get the unit to the middle of the pack, this team will be a playoff contender.

#7 Jacksonville Jaguars : Coach Liam Coen had Trevor Lawrence and the offense playing at an elite level for the second half of last season. With another step forward, this team can develop into a potential dynasty with their young core of players.

#6 Baltimore Ravens : The vibes surrounding this team have all been positive as new head coach Jesse Minter, along with new OC Declan Doyle, have the players and fans excited. If Lamar can return to his previous MVP-level form, this team should make quick work of the AFC North.

#5 Buffalo Bills : The new head coach isn't really new as he's been with the team for a few years. This is likely Josh Allen 's last shot to stake a claim to becoming the King of the North……East. The Bills defense needs to improve from last year's horrid showing, especially against the run.

#4 Los Angeles Rams : We had to ding them after the opening night loss. The Rams look to be one of the best teams in the league on paper, but the games aren't played on paper. Sometimes they're played in Australia. Once Aaron Donald is ready to roll, this defense is going to be filthy.

#3 Philadelphia Eagles : The offensive line is healthy and so is the defense. If Sean Mannion and Jalen Hurts are on the same page, this offense is going to be plenty strong enough to outpace their opponents each week. It will be interesting to see if they can handle business at home this week against Washington.

#2 Denver Broncos : This might be the best defense from top to bottom in the league. If Bo Nix can pick up where he left off last year and take another step forward, this can very well be the AFC representative in this year's final game.

#1 Seattle Seahawks: If you want to be the best, you've got to beat the best. Right now, this team is the best in the league until somebody comes in and knocks off their crown.

articles.title: GB's Taylor-Brown wins Czech leg of World Series
articles.summary: Great Britain's Georgia Taylor-Brown wins the women's event of the World Triathlon Championship Series in the Czech Republic.
articles.body:
Great Britain's Georgia Taylor-Brown produced a dominant display to win the final women's event of the regular World Championship Triathlon Series (WCTS) in the Czech Republic.

The 32-year-old finished the punishing hilly course at Karlovy Vary 36 seconds in front of the United States' Taylor Spivey, finishing the 1.5km swim, 40km bike ride and 10km run in two hours three minutes five seconds.

Germany's reigning champion Lisa Tertsch came third, one minute 28 seconds behind Taylor-Brown.

It was the Briton's best performance of the WCTS season and first victory on the tour since 2023.

She has concentrated on longer distances this season, with the 2020 Olympic silver medallist winning on the T100 tour in Spain in May - her best previous result in the WCTS this season was fourth in Samarkand in April.

Compatriot Beth Potter, who went into the event in second place in the overall standings, finished down in sixth, almost two-and-a-half minutes back.

Of the other British competitors, Kate Waugh was 10th, Sian Rainsley 14th and Olivia Mathias failed to finish.

Sunday's results meant that Potter was unable to capitalise on the absence of WCTS leader Cassandra Beaugrand of France, who chose not to compete.

Beaugrand leads the championship with a maximum 4,000 points going into the WCTS Grand Finals in Pontevedra, Spain, on 26 September.

Olympic champion Alex Yee heads the British challenge in the men's event on Sunday in Karlovy Vary, which is due to start at 14:00 BST.
